FERC Docket No. ER26-3380-000 
PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement Proposal 
NOVEC Protest 
 
 
 
 
Affidavit of Wilbur Rollins 
Northern Virginia Electric Cooperative, Inc.

Affidavit of Rollins 
Page 1 of 4 
 
 
AFFIDAVIT OF WILBUR ROLLINS ON BEHALF OF  
NORTHERN VIRGINIA ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC. 
Docket No. ER26-3380-000 
I. 
INTRODUCTION 
1 
Q. 
PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS. 
2 
A. 
My name is Wilbur Rollins. My business address is 10323 Lomond Dr., Manassas, VA, 
3 
20109. 
4 
Q. 
BY WHOM ARE YOU EMPLOYED AND IN WHAT POSITION? 
5 
A. 
I am employed by Northern Virginia Electric Cooperative, Inc. (“NOVEC”) as Senior Vice 
6 
President of Finance and Accounting. I have worked for NOVEC since March 1989 in the 
7 
finance and accounting department. I have been in my current position since 1998. Prior to 
8 
joining NOVEC, I was employed by Alabama Electric Cooperative, currently known as 
9 
Power South Energy Cooperative, beginning in September 1982. 
10 
II. 
PURPOSE OF THIS AFFIDAVIT 
11 
Q. 
WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR AFFIDAVIT IN THIS PROCEEDING? 
12 
A. 
I am providing information about the impact on NOVEC of the proposed collateral 
13 
requirements associated with PJM’s proposed Reliability Backstop Procurement (“RBP”). 
14 
III. 
PJM RELIABILITY BACKSTOP PROCUREMENT PROPOSAL 
15 
Q. 
PLEASE DESCRIBE NOVEC AND ITS CUSTOMERS? 
16 
A. 
NOVEC is a not-for-profit electric distribution cooperative organized and existing under 
17 
Virginia law. NOVEC is owned by its member retail customers and seeks to provide 
18 
reliable electric service to its retail customers at the lowest rate reasonably possible.  
19 
NOVEC is one of the largest electric distribution cooperatives in the country. Its peak 
20 
demand in 2025 was approximately 2,360 MW. NOVEC serves approximately 184,000 
21

Affidavit of Rollins 
Page 2 of 4 
 
 
retail customer meters, of which about 169,200 are residential, 15,000 are commercial, and 
1 
60 are large-load data centers. NOVEC sold approximately 14.65 million MWh of energy 
2 
in 2025, 10.75 million MWh of which was consumed by the data centers that NOVEC 
3 
serves. Thus, only 61 of NOVEC’s total number of customer meters consumed 73.4% of 
4 
the energy sold by NOVEC at retail in 2025.  
5 
Q. 
WHAT 
IS 
YOUR 
UNDERSTANDING 
OF 
THE 
RBP 
COLLATERAL 
6 
OBLIGATIONS? 
7 
A. 
PJM’s proposed section 18.5(b)(i)(B)(1), would require Load Serving Entities to post RBP 
8 
Collateral equal to $1.5 million multiplied by the allocated RBP Obligation MW. That 
9 
proposed tariff section would also allow PJM to require additional RBP Collateral “as 
10 
appropriate” pursuant to the Unreasonable Credit Risk provisions of Attachment Q. RBP 
11 
Collateral must be in the form of a cash deposit or a letter of credit.  
12 
Q. 
WHAT DO YOU ESTIMATE NOVEC’S RBP COLLATERAL REQUIREMENT 
13 
WILL BE? 
14 
A. 
Assuming no offsets and using the table provided in paragraph 46 of Ms. Croop’s affidavit, 
15 
I estimate that NOVEC’s RBP Collateral will be $1.95 billion ($1.5 million * 1,302.6 
16 
MW).  
17 
Q. 
WHAT 
IS 
YOUR 
OPINION 
OF 
THIS 
PROPOSED 
COLLATERAL 
18 
REQUIREMENT? 
19 
A. 
It is shockingly unreasonable. Putting aside the fact that PJM is designating a select few to 
20 
cure a PJM-wide problem, suddenly requiring NOVEC to post nearly $2 billion of 
21 
collateral is a tremendous burden that NOVEC may not even be able to meet, and is not 
22 
necessary to ensure NOVEC fulfills its obligations. 
23

Affidavit of Rollins 
Page 3 of 4 
 
 
Q. 
WHY IS IT NOT NECESSARY TO ENSURE NOVEC PAYS THE RBP 
1 
CHARGES? 
2 
A. 
NOVEC has an investment-grade credit rating. Further, to my knowledge, NOVEC has 
3 
always paid its obligations related to PJM membership. 
4 
Q. 
CAN YOU EXPLAIN WHY THE RBP COLLATERAL REQUIREMENT IS A 
5 
BURDEN TO NOVEC? 
6 
A. 
Yes. To give an idea of the relative impact on NOVEC, the RBP collateral amount exceeds 
7 
the $1.8 billion of assets on NOVEC’s balance sheets. I am uncertain whether financial 
8 
institutions would be willing to provide NOVEC with a letter of credit in an amount that 
9 
exceeds NOVEC’s assets. Even if NOVEC could procure a letter of credit, being so over-
10 
leveraged would severely damage NOVEC’s credit rating. NOVEC may not be able to 
11 
enter into bilateral wholesale energy and capacity transactions, where the sellers would 
12 
begin requiring greater credit assurance even though today they do not require NOVEC to 
13 
post collateral due to NOVEC’s strong credit rating. The resulting credit-support costs 
14 
associated with the bilateral transactions will increase power supply costs, which will be 
15 
passed onto retail customers. 
16 
Q. 
HOW ELSE WILL NOVEC BE HARMED? 
17 
A. 
NOVEC may not be able to borrow additional money for constructing infrastructure to 
18 
maintain reliability. NOVEC spends approximately $70 to $90 million annually on both 
19 
“end of life” replacements and necessary expansions, which would have to be curtailed. 
20 
Even if NOVEC could procure a letter of credit, the collateral obligation would come with 
21 
a minimum of $20 million in annual carrying costs that NOVEC would have to flow 
22 
through or include in its rates. NOVEC might be able to still borrow for any of these 
23

Affidavit of Rollins 
Page 4 of 4 
 
 
purposes, but it would be at a substantially higher cost that would affect rates and materially 
1 
impact NOVEC’s ratepayers. 
2 
Q. 
DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR AFFIDAVIT? 
3 
A. 
Yes.
4

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. 
Docket No. ER26-3380-000 
VERIFICATION OF WILBUR ROLLINS 
I, Wilbur Rollins, declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of 
America that that the information contained in the foregoing affidavit was prepared by me or 
under my supervision, and is true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information and 
belief. 
Date: 
2/ / 0-c& 
Wilbur Rollins
